steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Legal evaluation requires assessing the strengths and weaknesses of a law, principle or proposal and reaching a supported judgement | Key Fact: A balanced argument presents points on both sides — for and against — before reaching a conclusion; one-sided answers cannot access top mark bands | Key Fact: Always support your points with specific legal examples, cases or statistics — vague or generalised statements score poorly | Key Fact: When evaluating a legal rule, consider: how effectively it achieves its purpose, whether it is clear and certain, whether it is fair and just, and whether there are gaps or inconsistencies
